statement: Averaging volatility-normalised trend signals across several horizons (24h to 336h/720h) improves net risk-adjusted returns versus v0's single horizon.
mechanism: Development diagnostics show large horizon sensitivity (single-horizon variants ranged widely in development OOS Sharpe) and trading costs of ~0.32x |gross PnL| for v0. Horizon-specific noise is partly independent across horizons, so the average should keep the common trend premium while flipping sign less often, lowering turnover and costs.
alternatives: The trend premium lives at one horizon only; averaging dilutes it with noise horizons
Lower turnover is offset by slower reaction to reversals (larger drawdowns)
Any improvement is a development-period artefact (2020-2023 regimes)
prediction: Development walk-forward OOS Sharpe above v0's, fewer position changes than v0, and a validation improvement passing the frozen promotion rule; refuted if the development screen fails or validation P(delta Sharpe > 0) < 0.5.
novelty: Multi-horizon averaging is outside the offline grammar (single-horizon signals only); no prior task in any lab tested it.
